note: The Philippines' largest banks are BDO, Metrobank and BPI. BDO's site didn't answer this research (no connection, 2026-10-30), so BPI and Metrobank are written. BPI's credit card rates and fees page (read again 2026-10-30): each card's principal membership fee, charged after the first year of card ownership (written as waived for the first year, or the first twelve months for the monthly fees): Signature 5,500 pesos a year, Robinsons Cashback 2,500, Platinum Rewards 4,000, Gold Rewards 2,250, Amore Cashback 2,050, Rewards and Petron 1,550 (the Rewards Card this file has held since 2026-10-29), Family 1,350, Edge 110 a month, Omni 250 a month, eCredit and Free+ free; finance charges 3% a month (2.73% effective), 2.5% on the Free+; cash advances 3% a month and a flat 200-peso fee (not yet available on the Omni and Free+); spending in another currency 0.85% plus the network's 1%, written as 1.85% (the Free+ 2% plus 1%, written as 3%); the minimum payment 3.57% of the balance excluding the month's new transactions, at least 850 pesos, plus anything past due (written as 3.57% with an 850 floor); a late payment 850 pesos or the unpaid minimum if lower (written as 850); a returned cheque 100 pesos (the further 6% of the cheque isn't written). The Corporate Card isn't written. Metrobank's credit card rates and fees page (read 2026-10-30, rendered in a browser): each card's primary annual fee, waived for the first year: Titanium Mastercard, Rewards Plus Visa and Toyota Card 2,500 pesos, Toyota Platinum 2,800, Cashback Visa 3,500, Platinum Mastercard, Travel Platinum Visa and Femme Signature Visa 5,000, Travel Signature Visa 5,500, World Mastercard 6,000, Hype 1,500; the PSBank Credit Mastercard and M Free Mastercard waived for good; 3% a month on purchases and cash advances; a cash advance 200 pesos; the minimum payment 1,000 pesos or 3.5% of the balance plus any over-limit and past-due amounts, whichever is higher; over the limit 750 pesos; a returned cheque 1,500 pesos; spending in another currency a forex processing fee (2.50%; 0.85% World, 0.68% Travel Signature) plus a 1% cross-border service fee, written added (3.5%, 1.85%, 1.68%; the Hype card 2.5%, with no cross-border fee). The late payment fee the page gives (1,000 to 1,500 pesos or the unpaid minimum) takes effect only on 1 February 2027 and isn't written; the current one isn't stated. The Dollar Mastercard and ICON, with their own terms, aren't written. Wave 4 (2026-10-30): EastWest Bank, a large card issuer that publishes each card's fees on its card pages, is added in BDO's place (BDO's site still didn't answer; Security Bank's answers Cloudflare's block, RCBC's credit site a captcha, UnionBank's and PNB's 403, AUB's Incapsula, 2026-10-30). EastWest's fourteen personal credit card pages (read 2026-10-30), each card's fees and charges: the principal card's annual membership fee, Dolce Vita Titanium Mastercard 2,000 pesos, Gold Mastercard, Gold Visa and JCB Gold 2,500, JCB Platinum 3,500, Privilege Mastercard and Visa 1,500, each free its first year; foodpanda Visa 1,200; KrisFlyer Platinum Mastercard 4,000; KrisFlyer World Mastercard 5,000; Visa Platinum 4,000, waived automatically on 1.5 million pesos spent in the past twelve months (written as a spending waiver); the Platinum Mastercard and Priority Visa Infinite waived for good; the Puregold Always Panalo Visa 1,200 a year billed as 100 pesos a month (its waiver on 80,000 pesos of cross-border and online spending, a kind of spending the game doesn't count, isn't written). Every card: interest 3% a month (36% effective a year), written as 3% a month; a cash advance 200 pesos and 3% a month; a late payment 1,500 pesos or the unpaid minimum, whichever is lower (written as 1,500); over the limit 800; a returned check 1,500; a foreign transaction service fee of 2.50% (Visa or Mastercard's assessment and EastWest's fee together), 2.00% on the JCB cards, 3.00% on the Privilege and Puregold cards and 1.70% on the KrisFlyer cards and Priority Visa Infinite. The quasi-cash fee and the retrieval and replacement fees aren't written; no minimum payment or grace period is stated on the pages. Wave 5 (2026-10-30), minimum payments: EastWest's credit card fees and charges page (read 2026-10-30): the minimum is 3.5% of the total statement balance (fees, charges and instalments included), plus any past-due and over-limit amount, or 200 pesos, whichever is higher; written on its fourteen cards as 3.5% with a 200 floor.
